question: Who tastes the ketaki fragrance — bee or fly — in supreme Bhairava worship?
premises: who approaches undivided true being as self-principle
in ketaki fragrance the bee is connoisseur, not the fly
in supreme nondual Bhairava worship someone delights, impelled by Mahesa
inference: The qualified tastes; the unqualified cannot — delight is Maheśa-impelled.
uncertainties: closing verse; bee/fly kept as given
plain_english: Who approaches undivided true-being as self-principle — in ketaki-flower fragrance intensely the bee is connoisseur, not the fly; in supreme nondual Bhairava worship someone delights, impelled by Mahesa.
